summary: Deferred kernel swap leads to request timeout for extremely large prompt + high max_tokens
description: Issue summary: Customer reports repeated request timeouts for single inference calls where the prompt is ~210k tokens and max_tokens=100k. The underlying serving runtime appears to trigger a deferred kernel swap during generation which introduces a multi-second stall; client times out at 120s. Impact: Production feature at Helios Labs (analytics pipeline) experiences ~30% failure rate for these long-batch jobs, causing downstream data gaps and an escalated support case. Environment: Dedicated pool in prod-us-east, customer pinned to a specific instance group with mixed GPU types (A100 + A10G). Observed behavior: Requests hang during token generation after ~65k generated tokens; server logs show a queued "kernel_swap_pending" event followed by extended GC/serialization activity, then 504 to client. Expected behavior: Continuous generation without multi-second stalls; kernel transitions (if any) should be amortized or performed off the hot path. Additional constraints: Customer requires these long-context runs for transcript stitching and is unwilling to significantly lower max_tokens without alternative cost mitigations.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use Helios Labs test account with dedicated pool in prod-us-east.
2) POST /v1/generate with model rw-opt-13b-int8, prompt length ~210k tokens, max_tokens=100000, streaming=false, timeout=120s.
3) Observe generation proceeds to ~65k output tokens then stalls; client receives 504 after 120s.
4) Re-run with max_tokens=20k and identical prompt — completes successfully within expected time.
5) Replay with streaming=true shows intermittent partial chunks then final cutoff at same time boundary.
logs: 2026-03-10T14:16:53Z [gateway] WARN request_id=abc123 returning 504 to client after stall
comments: Support (Priya): Initial triage — reproduced with Helios test creds, escalating to SRE to check kernel swap path and model container memory pressure.

SRE (Marco): Noted that instance group is mixed GPU; requesting allocation and metrics for the particular worker (worker-id i-0a1b2c3d). Hypothesis: deferred kernel swap (when switching execution kernels for long KV cache segments) blocks the generation thread while copying large KV pages.
Customer (Helios Ops): Can we get a short-term workaround? Dropping max_tokens to 50k impacts our downstream stitching but is acceptable if we can parallelize client-side for the next 48 hours.

Support (Priya): Provided suggested workaround: (A) set max_tokens<=50k, (B) enable streaming=true + chunked_finalizer to flush partial outputs earlier, (C) schedule reroute to a homogeneous A100-only pool. Customer accepted A and B while we investigate C.
investigation_notes: SRE observation: kernel_swap_pending events correlate with large KV cache sizes (~1.2GB) and occur when runtime decides to change execution kernel for the next decode block.
Profiling: the swap path performs a device-to-device memcpy followed by CPU-side serialization for checkpointing which blocks the generation thread for 3-6s under load.
Allocator metrics: peak GPU memory usage spikes just prior to the swap; we observed transient OOM-safety paths that trigger additional serialization and slowdowns.
Scheduler note: mixed-GPU worker pools increase probability of hitting a less optimized kernel path that requires swap; homogeneous pools did not reproduce on A100-only nodes (internal test).
Repro attempts: Reproduced on dedicated pool instance i-0a1b2c3d (mixed GPUs), did not reproduce on reserved A100-only test cluster.
Related: See linked issues SUP-29541 (kv-cache stalls) and SUP-53721 (backpressure on large max_tokens).
resolution_notes: Workaround applied: advised customer to set max_tokens<=50k and enable streaming+chunked_finalizer. Customer implemented and failure rate dropped from ~30% to <2%.
Short-term fix: moved Helios routing to homogeneous A100 worker pool for next 72 hours (manual routing) which eliminated kernel-swap stalls in validation runs.

Medium-term mitigation (in progress): runtime change to perform kernel swap asynchronously off the generation hot path and to prefetch/lock KV pages to avoid CPU serialization during active generation. PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1124.
Follow-ups: schedule postmortem with SRE + Runtime + Customer success to discuss SLA uplift and plan for automatic pool selection when model+prompt sizes exceed threshold.
Status: partial mitigation in prod for this customer; engineering roadmap item created to harden kernel swap path.
